content.title: About
content.content: Corn oil is extracted from the germ of corn kernels. It has a light yellow color, neutral taste and aroma. The oil is rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids, especially linoleic (omega‑6) and oleic (monounsaturated) acids. It is widely used in cooking, the food industry and cosmetics.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn oil is one of the most popular vegetable oils in the United States.
Unlike olive oil, corn oil remains stable at room temperature for a longer period without rancidity.
It contains more vitamin E than most other vegetable oils.
The oil is often used in the production of margarines and mayonnaise because of its excellent emulsifying properties.
Cold‑pressed corn oil exists, but most commercial products are refined and purified.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains polyunsaturated fatty acids
items.content: Linoleic acid helps maintain normal blood cholesterol levels.

items.title: Supports skin health
items.content: The presence of vitamin E and fatty acids makes the oil beneficial in moisturizers and skin‑protective products.

items.title: High energy density
items.content: Corn oil provides a concentrated source of calories, useful for increased energy needs.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with animal fats, corn oil contains less saturated fatty acids, making it more suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: High omega‑6 content
items.content: Excessive intake of omega‑6 fatty acids without adequate omega‑3 balance may promote inflammatory processes.

items.title: Refining and chemical residues
items.content: Most commercial corn oil is refined, often using solvents such as hexane.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products, including the oil.

items.title: Oxidation when heated
items.content: Prolonged heating can cause the oil to oxidize and form harmful compounds.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Corn oil is suitable for frying, baking and making salad dressings. Its neutral flavor allows it to be used in pastries, marinades and sauces. In cosmetics, it is used as a moisturizing ingredient in creams and hair masks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store corn oil in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator to slow oxidation. Discard the oil if it develops a sharp odor or becomes cloudy.
